description: Complete-backup retention configuration (I5, issue #57). Single source of truth mirrored by convex/operations/backups/slot.ts; tests/i5 asserts the two cannot drift. Frequent complete sets are kept 48 hours; daily complete sets (the first slot of each UTC day) are kept through day 14. Media objects are pooled and shared across sets: collection is reference-aware and deletes an object only when NO surviving manifest references it. Deleted-source content cannot survive backups beyond 30 days: the retention invariant (no set outlives 14 days) holds by construction and is asserted at runtime and in tests, so a future retention extension that would break the 30-day bound fails loudly instead of silently keeping purged bytes.

schedule.note: Every 15 minutes, the accepted cadence. Frequency is NEVER silently reduced to fit a plan: a plan-limit breach is a loud typed failure plus owner decision (see plan-limits.json and the 400/500 PLN cost alerts), never a quiet schedule change. The cadence is owned in TWO places that tests keep equal: this file and the backup Container's cron trigger (apps/backup-worker/wrangler.jsonc).

daily.window: through day 14 (selection: the first 15-minute slot of each UTC day)

deletedContent.enforcement: purged-source media is excluded from NEW sets at build time (I4 ledger); every set expires within 14 days, so backup content cannot outlive 30 days; the invariant retention <= 30d is asserted at runtime (beginRun refuses on violation) and in tests/i5

freshness.measuredFrom: database snapshot time (snapshotAtMs of the newest VERIFIED manifest), never completion time
freshness.alerting: ops.backup.stale diagnostic (deduped per episode) + backup.job heartbeats every attempt (I2 silence detection fires at 3x15m, before the one-hour limit)

orphanCollection.note: interrupted runs' pool objects (never referenced by any manifest) are collected after a 48h grace window
